summary: This is a Mol Labs public hypothesis card (N12) proposing a pre-registered assay to test whether a combined selective MAO-A inhibitor (clorgyline-class) + selective MAO-B inhibitor (selegiline/rasagiline-class) fails to match methylene blue (MB) rescue of memory retention in a cytochrome oxidase (COX)-inhibitor amnestic model. The document is a research-discussion/propose-assay record with a NEGATIVE status label, meaning the dual selective MAOI combo is predicted to underperform MB. No experiments have been run (execution_status=NOT_RUN); the claim is a prediction grounded in prior literature and the logic of prior cards N10/N11.

content_blocks.title: Document Metadata and Status
content_blocks.content: Card ID: N12. Status: NEGATIVE (prediction). Policy: PUBLIC_REPORT_ONLY. Risk class: research-discussion. Tags: nootropics, brain-longevity. Topic: neuroscience-brain. Vault hold: no. Execution status: NOT_RUN. FTO status: UNKNOWN. Kill cost tier: 1. Time to refute: 4 weeks. IP class: redox-vs-MAO. Document date: 2026-09-26.

content_blocks.title: Core Claim
content_blocks.content: On a pre-registered cytochrome-oxidase (COX) inhibitor amnestic retention assay where parent methylene blue (MB) restores memory, a combined selective MAO-A inhibitor (clorgyline-class) + selective MAO-B inhibitor (selegiline/rasagiline-class) fails to match that rescue — retention Δ ≤70% of MB (or outside a pre-registered MB-equivalence band). This is a PREDICTION; no experiment has been run.

content_blocks.title: Scientific Rationale and Mechanism
content_blocks.content: MB restores retention after COX inhibition and is a preferential reversible MAO-A inhibitor. Selective MAO-A (clorgyline-class) and MAO-B (rasagiline/selegiline-class) tools exist but no published dual-combo COX-amnestic retention head-to-head (H2H) vs MB exists. The dual-isoform escape hypothesis: N10 (MAO-A alone) and N11 (MAO-B alone) leave open that A+B together could match MB; N12 is designed to close that escape. Competing caveats include occupancy/exposure matching (underperformance could reflect under-dosing), and that MAO IC50 ≠ brain rescue pharmacodynamics.

content_blocks.title: Why It Matters / Scientific Context
content_blocks.content: Closes dual-isoform escape on the Gonzalez-Lima COX-amnestic assay after N10 (selective MAO-A alone) and N11 (selective MAO-B alone). If COX-amnestic rescue were dual-MAO-driven, A+B should match MB; preferential redox/COX-facing framing and MB's preferential MAO-A enzyme profile both predict the dual selective combo underperforms. Distinct from N10/N11 (single-isoform), N5 (MAO-A generic WM), N8 (Azure B), N9 (redox-dead) — none ran dual selective MAOI vs parent MB on this assay.

content_blocks.title: Prior Art / Literature Baseline
content_blocks.content:
Four key prior art references cited:
1. PMID 12384216 (Callaway/Gonzalez-Lima, 2002): Low-dose MB restores spatial memory retention impaired by a cytochrome oxidase inhibitor — no dual selective MAOI arm.
2. PMID 21087672 (Rojas/Gonzalez-Lima, 2011): MB beneficial network effects in an amnestic model (metabolic/network framing) — no dual selective MAOI arm.
3. PMID 17721552 (Ramsay, 2007): MB potent reversible preferential MAO-A inhibition (serotonin-toxicity prediction) — enzyme/isoform prior, not COX-amnestic dual H2H.
4. PMID 26142126 (Weinreb, 2015): Rasagiline (selective MAO-B-i) improves cognitive deficits and related cascades in aged mice — MAO-B tool prior, not dual-combo COX-amnestic retention vs MB.

content_blocks.title: Baseline Measured / Evidence Status
content_blocks.content: MB COX-amnestic/amnestic-network rescue: LITERATURE (PMID 12384216; 21087672). MB preferential reversible MAO-A inhibition: LITERATURE (PMID 17721552). Rasagiline selective MAO-B tool: LITERATURE (PMID 26142126). Dual selective MAO-A-i + MAO-B-i vs parent MB on same COX-amnestic rescue/retention panel: UNKNOWN (soft-complete dual selective MAOI∩MB∩COX-amnestic = 0). ≤70% MB-equivalence fail: PREDICTION. N5–N11 do not already prove this — N10/N11 single arms leave dual escape open.

content_blocks.title: Actionable Limitations
content_blocks.content:
1. Do not treat N5–N11 as proving N12 — N10/N11 are single-isoform arms (H2H UNKNOWN); N5 was A-biased/generic WM; N8/N9 ran metabolite/redox-dead arms, not dual selective MAOI combo; soft-complete empty ≠ demonstrated dual-combo failure on COX-amnestic.
2. MAO IC50 ≠ brain rescue PD — Ramsay is preferential MAO-A enzyme inhibition; Weinreb is aged-cognition/cascades; clorgyline is monoamine/affective — none is dual-combo COX-amnestic retention vs MB.
3. Dual-isoform escape + occupancy matching — do not collapse N10+N11 into dual proof; underperformance could be under-dosing relative to MB's MAO profile; assay MAO-A/B occupancy/monoamine readout without a dosing card; use same COX-inhibitor amnestic class where parent MB restores. No dosing specified.

content_blocks.title: Refutation Criteria
content_blocks.content: On the pre-registered COX-inhibitor amnestic retention assay, the dual selective MAO-A-i + MAO-B-i matches parent MB within the MB-equivalence band (retention Δ >70% of MB or inside band) — especially under exposure/MAO-A/B-occupancy-matched conditions — so dual-MAO-necessity for metabolic-memory rescue survives and redox-required framing fails.

content_blocks.content: Execution status: NOT_RUN. FTO status: UNKNOWN. Method: propose-assay. Kill cost tier: 1 (cheap). Time to refute: 4 weeks. IP class: redox-vs-MAO. Vault hold: no. Related prior: N5–N11 (single-isoform/metabolite/redox-dead ≠ dual selective MAOI COX-amnestic proof; N10+N11 ≠ dual proof).

key_findings: Execution status is NOT_RUN — this is a proposed assay/prediction, not a completed experiment; no empirical data has been generated.

Core prediction (NEGATIVE): Combined selective MAO-A inhibitor (clorgyline-class) + selective MAO-B inhibitor (selegiline/rasagiline-class) will fail to match methylene blue (MB) rescue of memory retention in a COX-inhibitor amnestic model (predicted retention Δ ≤70% of MB).
No published dual-combo COX-amnestic retention H2H vs MB exists (soft-complete = 0; UNKNOWN status for key variable).

Four literature anchors cited: PMID 12384216 (MB restores spatial memory after COX inhibition), PMID 21087672 (MB network effects in amnestic model), PMID 17721552 (MB preferential reversible MAO-A inhibition), PMID 26142126 (rasagiline selective MAO-B tool in aged mice).
N10 (MAO-A alone) and N11 (MAO-B alone) single-isoform cards leave dual-isoform escape open; N12 is designed to close that escape.
Key competing caveat: underperformance of dual MAOI could reflect under-dosing/occupancy mismatch rather than true mechanistic failure; MAO IC50 ≠ brain rescue pharmacodynamics.
Kill cost is tier 1 (cheap); estimated time to refute is 4 weeks, indicating low experimental burden.
FTO status is UNKNOWN; IP class is redox-vs-MAO.
TRL assessment: TRL 1 — concept/hypothesis only; no experimental data generated; assay proposed but not executed.
